Definition: from G1321; (subjectively) instructed, or (objectively) communicated by teaching:--taught, which … teacheth.
BiblicalUsage: Taught of God is the promise for everyone who hears and learns of the Father, and the word stands twice for it. Paul says the words he speaks are taught not by man's wisdom but by the Holy Spirit, and Jesus says all who have heard and learned of the Father come to Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being taught of God is the quiet miracle behind every conversion; no man comes to Christ by argument alone; the Father teaches, and those who hear Him come.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
